Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which portfolio artifact best shows speaking organization?

answer.text: A. A random image with no explanation.

feedback.text: This does not show speaking organization. A portfolio artifact should provide evidence of a communication skill.

answer.text: B. A speaking outline with purpose, audience, main points, and transitions.

feedback.text: Correct. This artifact shows how the speaker planned a clear spoken message for an audience.

answer.text: C. A list of favorite topics with no speech plan.

feedback.text: This may show interests, but it does not prove speaking organization or readiness.

answer.text: D. A blank slide deck template.

feedback.text: A template alone does not show communication skill. The artifact must include meaningful planning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.01

Which reflection best explains why a slide deck belongs in a communication portfolio?

answer.text: A. I included it because it has colors.

feedback.text: This focuses on decoration, not communication skill. Reflection should explain what the artifact proves.

answer.text: B. I included it because it took a long time.

feedback.text: Effort matters, but a portfolio reflection should identify the skill demonstrated by the artifact.

answer.text: C. I included it because every portfolio needs slides.

feedback.text: This is generic and does not explain the specific communication value.

answer.text: D. I included it because it shows how I matched visuals to spoken points for a specific audience.

feedback.text: Correct. This reflection connects the artifact to presentation planning and audience awareness.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.01

Which artifact best shows research-supported communication?

answer.text: A. Briefing notes that include a research question, source evidence, and explanation.

feedback.text: Correct. This artifact shows how research was selected and explained for a communication purpose.

answer.text: B. A personal opinion paragraph with no source support.

feedback.text: This does not show research-supported communication because it lacks evidence from a source.

answer.text: C. A decorative title page for the portfolio.

feedback.text: A title page can organize the portfolio, but it does not show research skill by itself.

answer.text: D. A list of websites with no explanation.

feedback.text: A list alone does not show how sources support a message. The artifact needs source explanation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which portfolio explanation best shows digital communication skill?

answer.text: A. This flyer looks nice, so it is useful.

feedback.text: This is too vague. Digital communication should be explained through audience, purpose, format, and clarity.

answer.text: B. This digital flyer uses headings, readable contrast, and a clear sign-up step for the audience.

feedback.text: Correct. This explanation names specific design choices and connects them to audience use.

answer.text: C. This file is digital, so it automatically shows skill.

feedback.text: Being digital is not enough. The artifact must show audience-aware communication choices.

answer.text: D. This announcement has many words, so it is complete.

feedback.text: More words do not guarantee clarity. Digital publication should be organized for the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

What should a portfolio introduction do for the reviewer?

answer.text: A. Hide the purpose so the reviewer discovers it later.

feedback.text: This makes the portfolio harder to understand. The introduction should orient the audience.

answer.text: B. List files without explaining their communication value.

feedback.text: A list alone does not show mastery. The reviewer needs to know why artifacts were selected.

answer.text: C. Explain the portfolio purpose, audience, and skills the reviewer should notice.

feedback.text: Correct. This prepares the reviewer to understand how the artifacts show communication growth and readiness.

answer.text: D. Focus only on how difficult the work felt.

feedback.text: Reflection can mention growth, but the introduction should focus on purpose, audience, and demonstrated skills.
